Application No. 22651-T1 — Substitute

17-13-0303-C(1) Substitute Type 1 Narrative & Plans — 2501 N. Clark St, Chicago, IL

Proposed Zoning: B3-5 Community Shopping District
Lot Area: Approx. 6,550 sq. ft.

Proposed Land Use: The Applicant is proposing to develop the subject property with a six-story
mixed-use building containing approximately 3,775 sq. ft. of retail space at
grade, and a total of twenty (20) residential units on the floors above grade.
The subject property is a Transit Served Location. Pursuant to Sec. 17-13-
0303-D optional Administrative Adjustment and Variation and pursuant to
Secs. 17-13-1101-B, 17-13-1101-D, 17-13-1003-L, and 17-13-1003-EE, of
the Chicago Zoning Ordinance, the Applicant is seeking to reduce the rear
setback required for floors containing residential uses from the required 30
ft. to 10 ft., waive the loading berth requirement, reduce the off-street
parking requirement to zero, increase the allowable building height from 70
ft. to 71 ft.-6 inches, and any other relief needed to permit the proposed Plan
Set.

(A) _ The Project’s Floor Area Ratio: 32,750 square feet (5.0 FAR)

(B) The Project’s Density (Minimum Lot Area Per D.U.): 327.5 square feet per D.U.
(20 residential units)

(C) The amount of off-street parking: 0 parking spaces

*The subject property is a designated Transit Served Location (Clark St.. Bus
Route). Pursuant to Sec. 17-13-1003-EE, the Applicant is seeking to reduce the
required number of off-street parking spaces to zero.

(D) Setbacks:
a. Front Setback: 12 inches
b. Side Setbacks:
North Side: 12 inches
South Side: zero
c. *Rear Setback: 10 feet

*Pursuant to Sec. 17-13-1101-B, the Applicant is seeking to reduce’the rear setback
for floors containing residential uses from the required 30 feet to 10 feet.

(E) Building Height: 71 feet and 6 inches

*Pursuant to Sec. 17-13-1003-L, the Applicant is seeking to increase the allowable
building height from 70 ft. to 71 ft.-6 inches.

Sec. 17-3-0308 Criteria for Transit-Served Locations — Supplemental Narrative Zoning Analysis

|. The subject property is a designated Transit Served Location per Sec. 17-10-0102-B
because it is located along the Clark Street CTA Bus Line Corridor roadway segment. The
proposed mixed-use building will contain retail space at grade and twenty (20) residential
units above. The proposed mixed-use building is landlocked and will not be supported by
off-street parking spaces. Pursuant to Section 17-13-1003-EE, the Applicant is seeking to
permit an decrease in the number of required off-street parking spaces to zero.

2. The proposed building design complies with the main building door and entryway design
standards provided by Sec. 17-4-0504 because the front setback will be at the front of the
property line, the entrance widths do not exceed 12 ft., the entrance depths do not exceed
the entrance width, the entrance is not more than two-stories in height, the proposed
building elevations comply with the window transparency requirements, and the front
doors to the building are located along N. Clark St. and St. James Ave.

3. The Transit Friendly Development Guide defines ‘transit friendly development’ as
development which is oriented towards and integrated with adjacent transit. The proposed
mixed-use building incorporates accessibility and connectivity to mass transit based on its
location near the Clark Street Bus Route. The Applicant believes the project will help
improve and activate the pedestrian way along N. Clark St. for residents and other
commuters traveling in the subject area.

4, The proposed mixed-use building will contain twenty (20) dwelling units above grade level
and will not be supported by off-street parking. The Applicant is seeking administrative
approval to permit the parking reduction pursuant to the eTOD Ordinance. A minimum of
twenty (20) bicycle parking spaces will be provided onsite.

5, The Applicant believes the proposed mixed-use building will provide appropriate density
in the subject neighborhood. More specifically, the project will complement the already
active stretch of mixed-use property located along N. Clark St. Based on the subject
property’s proximity to a designated bus route (Clark Street CTA Bus Line), and its offer
of at least twenty (20) bicycle parking spaces, the Applicant believes the project provides
transit options and otherwise complies with the Travel Demand Study and Management
Plan rules promulgated by the Department of Transportation by serving an area in need.
